question: What is the difference between a basis and a spanning set?
direct_answer: A basis spans the space with no redundant vectors.
expanded_answer: A spanning set may contain extra vectors, but a basis is a minimal spanning set whose vectors are linearly independent. That means none of them can be written as a combination of the others. A basis gives unique coordinates for vectors in the space, which is why it is the cleanest way to describe dimensionality.
key_points: A basis has no redundant vectors
common_wrong_ideas: Any spanning set is a basis
A basis is unique for a given vector space
